blocks.text: Architecting a Multi-Cloud Strategy for a Mission-Critical Logistics Platform
Logistics
Client
A provider of Employee Transportation Management Systems (ETMS) and real-time vehicle tracking applications.
Ambition
To mitigate the business risks of vendor lock-in by adopting a multi-cloud strategy for their mission-critical fleet management applications.
Outcome
Architected and executed a seamless migration of their core applications to Google Cloud, providing greater control, improving resilience, and achieving significant cost savings.
The Ambition
A provider of Employee Transportation Management Systems (ETMS) and real-time vehicle tracking applications.
The Challenge

Relying solely on a single cloud provider posed significant risks of pricing changes, technology deprecation, or outages that could impact their entire operation. Their existing cloud vendor could not provide the level of control over the application infrastructure that they required to innovate and operate with confidence.
The Architectural Blueprint

The client's ambition was to build a resilient and future-proof infrastructure for their mission-critical applications. They needed to have more control over their technology stack and pricing, and avoid the risks associated with being dependent on a single cloud provider.
Ambition, Realized

The migration to Google Cloud was a strategic success. It immediately addressed their core challenge of vendor lock-in, providing greater resilience and business continuity. The move also delivered significant cost savings without compromising performance, thanks to Google Cloud's cost-effective offerings and our resource management strategies. The new environment gave them the control and flexibility they needed to continue innovating.
Key Business Impact
Mitigated Business Risk by Adopting a Multi-Cloud Strategy
Achieved Significant Cost Savings without Compromising Performance
Increased Control & Flexibility over Application Infrastructure
Ensured Business Continuity for Mission-Critical Applications
